_provenance.what: copaw Tool Guard regex rule set (dangerous_shell_commands.yaml) exported unchanged from a live AgentTeams worker container; the only rule file RuleBasedToolGuardian loads by default (_DEFAULT_RULE_FILES).
_provenance.export_command: docker exec agentteams-worker-agt-worker-dfb8a4cda6f7 sh -c '/opt/venv/standard/bin/python -c "import json, yaml; print(json.dumps(yaml.safe_load(open(\"/opt/venv/standard/lib/python3.11/site-packages/copaw/security/tool_guard/rules/dangerous_shell_commands.yaml\", encoding=\"utf-8\"))))"'
_provenance.match_semantics: copaw/security/tool_guard/guardians/rule_guardian.py GuardRule: a rule applies when tool_name is in `tools` and the parameter name is in `params`; the parameter value is str()-ed; if any exclude_pattern matches (re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE).search) the rule is skipped; otherwise the first pattern that matches with re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE).search is a finding of the rule's severity. HIGH and CRITICAL findings make the call unsafe and trigger the room approval flow. Rules with disabled_rules in config.json are dropped; the live worker config has none.
_provenance.not_covered: FilePathToolGuardian (copaw/security/tool_guard/guardians/file_guardian.py) is not a regex rule set: it blocks paths under security.file_guard.sensitive_files (default: the worker's secret dir). The helper's relative paths never resolve there.
_provenance.why: spec D-21 / spike S-1: the vendored copaw source under components/agentteams carries only the ToolGuardConfig model, not the rules; the wave-0 helper name rm-work.sh hit TOOL_CMD_DANGEROUS_RM on every shell call.

rules.description: Shell command contains 'rm' which may cause data loss
rules.remediation: Confirm with the user before removing files or directories

rules.description: Shell command contains 'mv' which may move or overwrite files unexpectedly
rules.remediation: Confirm with the user before moving or renaming files

rules.description: Detects low-level disk formatting or wiping commands
rules.remediation: Block operation. Agents should not format or overwrite raw block devices.

rules.description: Detects classic Bash fork bombs and mass process termination
rules.remediation: Block immediately. These commands will crash the host system.

rules.description: Detects 'curl | bash' patterns used to download and immediately execute remote payloads
rules.remediation: Confirm with user. Agents should inspect scripts before executing them.

rules.description: Detects attempts to establish reverse shells or unauthorized network tunnels
rules.remediation: Block operation. Agents do not need to bind interactive shells to network sockets.

rules.description: Detects access to cron jobs, SSH keys, or sudo permissions (including reads and modifications)
rules.remediation: Confirm with user. Treat any access to credential and scheduling files as sensitive and restrict when possible.

rules.description: Detects global permission downgrades (chmod 777) or setting immutable flags
rules.remediation: Prompt for confirmation. Suggest least-privilege permission models.

rules.description: Detects execution of base64 encoded strings passed directly to a shell interpreter
rules.remediation: Block execution. Agents should use plain text commands.

rules.description: Detects system reboot or shutdown commands that will terminate the host system
rules.remediation: Block operation. Agents should not restart or shutdown the system.

rules.description: Detects service management commands that can disrupt system services
rules.remediation: Confirm with user. Restarting services may cause downtime or data loss.

rules.description: Detects process termination commands that may kill critical processes
rules.remediation: Confirm with user. Killing processes may cause data loss or system instability.

rules.description: Detects privilege escalation attempts using sudo, su, doas, pkexec, or runas
rules.remediation: Block operation. Agents should not execute commands with elevated privileges.
